environment.description: AWS Lambda function running in account 444555666777 within OU 'ou-ab12-workloads' under organization o-abc123def4. The execution role 'ProvisionerLambdaRole' has the same IAM policies. However, the role has an attached permission boundary policy 'arn:aws:iam::444555666777:policy/LambdaProvisionerBoundary' which uses a conditional deny with StringNotLike on the iam:AttachUserPolicy action restricting PolicyArn to 'arn:aws:iam::444555666777:policy/team-*'. Additionally, the OU has SCP 'RestrictPrivilegeEscalation' (ID: p-a1b2c3d4e5) which contains an explicit Deny on sts:AssumeRole where the role path does not match '/service-roles/cross-account-*' using aws:ResourceTag/AllowLambdaAssume condition key. The SCP also denies lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration unless the principal tag 'deployment-pipeline' equals 'true', which is not set on the Lambda execution role. Note: the permission boundary alone would not prevent the sts:AssumeRole or lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration paths; the SCP alone would not prevent the iam:AttachUserPolicy escalation with AdministratorAccess. Both controls together close all three escalation vectors.

permission_boundary.effect: Deny iam:AttachUserPolicy unless PolicyArn matches arn:aws:iam::444555666777:policy/team-*

scp.name: RestrictPrivilegeEscalation
statements: Deny lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration unless principal tag deployment-pipeline=true
